historical_reviews.deepseek: Its single-vendor/single-controller shortcut can select an internal M.2 drive and falsely satisfy an E1.S-specific PCIe check.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly treats the textually similar M.2 row as context only and binds collection to this exact code, backplane topology and recipe.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code/source search found no earlier V3.1 record for this identity; the row-1751 review is deliberately non-substitutable.
historical_reviews.v3_1: For E1.S, endpoint identity must follow the front bay through backplane or PCIe-switch topology to the downstream BDF and controller serial. Upstream switch-port speed cannot substitute for downstream drive-link state, and a shared vendor ID cannot prove that every bay endpoint is present.

original_test_intent: Verify each E1.S drive endpoint's PCI vendor/device identity and negotiated PCIe speed, width and bandwidth against the E1.S-specific platform recipe.
original_method: Verify the exact chassis/backplane configuration, enumerate the full numeric PCI topology, map each populated E1.S bay through any switch/downstream port to its controller BDF and serial, capture complete LnkCap/LnkSta/error context at the drive endpoint, and compare row-specific IDs and link values without reusing M.2 evidence or changing PCIe/storage state.
manual_activity: The E1.S platform owner approves this code's bay/backplane/switch-to-controller BDF map, expected IDs and per-bay negotiated-link criteria.
required_inputs: Expected generation, width and bandwidth per endpoint
Verified host-key SSH with secret-safe authentication
safety_requirements: Use read-only lspci and NVMe identify operations
Do not reuse M.2 row results
Do not treat upstream switch-link state as the drive endpoint
Never expose credentials or disable host verification
Do not reset, retrain, remove, rescan or write devices
Preserve full outputs and exit status
agent_execution_scope: Confirm exact row and platform identity
Collect full PCI topology and numeric inventory
Resolve each approved E1.S bay to its downstream endpoint and controller serial
Capture per-endpoint verbose link and error status
Compare IDs and normalized actual bandwidth to the E1.S recipe
Report per-bay discrepancies without mutation or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve expected IDs and link thresholds
Resolve switch topology, alternate devices and optional bays

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The vendor filter and first NVMe controller do not identify E1.S bay endpoints, can select the M.2 device covered by row 1751, omit complete numeric enumeration, and use unsafe/fragile SSH quoting.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Using verified SSH, collect complete `lspci -nn` topology and `lspci -s <approved-E1.S-endpoint-BDF> -nn -vvv` plus read-only controller identity for every mapped bay; compare endpoint LnkSta/LnkCap and IDs to this row's SPEC.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Every E1.S disk endpoint, all four stated PCIe properties and the 10-minute source estimate remain in scope.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Produce a bay-keyed path of backplane/switch/downstream BDF/controller serial with numeric IDs, LnkCap, LnkSta, error status and calculated bandwidth for each E1.S drive.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes form-factor and row identity explicit, distinguishes upstream from downstream links, and eliminates hardcoded vendor/controller shortcuts.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: The text matches the M.2 row, but its Test Set changes the physical targets; reusing an M.2 endpoint or switch uplink can pass while an E1.S bay is missing or downtrained.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Collection is non-destructive, yet incorrect switch/downstream mapping can approve the wrong link; this check does not measure I/O throughput.

project_override_considerations: Supply current backplane and PCIe-switch routing after BIOS/bifurcation changes, the downstream BDF per E1.S bay, allowed alternate IDs and exact negotiated generation/width/bandwidth rules for this V002 row.
expected_evidence: Exact code/SUT/BIOS/backplane identity and row-specific E1.S SPEC
Verified SSH provenance, tool versions and timestamps
Complete PCI topology, per-endpoint verbose lspci and controller identity outputs
Per-bay ID, LnkCap/LnkSta, bandwidth and error-context comparison distinct from row 1751
Preserved logs, no-mutation audit, mismatch disposition and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Within this row, Test Set, Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently define E1.S PCIe verification. Matching body text in the M.2 row represents a parallel form-factor case, not an intrinsic source contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The E1.S purpose and read-only operation are clear; the row-specific topology and SPEC are identifiable prerequisites, so classification is REQUIRES.

review_improvement: Prevents text duplication from collapsing E1.S and M.2 coverage and requires the actual downstream link for every front-bay endpoint.
independent_technical_reasoning: A switched E1.S topology may expose both an uplink and multiple downstream links. Healthy uplink bandwidth does not prove each drive link is present or trained correctly. Because the source body is reused from the M.2 case, the Test Set and physical routing map are decisive Source Identity elements: evidence must terminate at each E1.S controller serial and cannot be copied across form factors.
